title: checks.config.json
description: Per-repo configuration for the aide-checks package. The package is never forked per repo; every difference lives here. Every exclusion carries a reason.

include.description: MUST contain docs/** and README.md (spec §4.1): scanners commonly skip documentation paths, and NEXUS-C116 lived exactly there.

exclusion_reasons.description: one entry per exclude pattern. Excluding a path because it is noisy is not a reason.

allow_fields.description: Field names whose assigned value is a domain identifier, not a credential (e.g. idempotency_key, feature_key). Suppresses a finding only when gitleaks matched that field, NOT the path: the file stays fully scanned, so a real secret elsewhere in it — or on the same line — still fails. This exists because spec §3 forbids excluding a path for noise, and a committed evidence dump is exactly where a real leak also lands. Every entry requires a matching allow_fields_reasons entry or the check exits 2.

allow_fields_reasons.description: One recorded reason per allow_fields entry. Required: the check refuses to run (exit 2) on an entry with no reason. An allowlist nobody has to justify grows until the scanner means nothing.

patterns.description: This repo's own worktree convention, read from its .gitignore history — not assumed (spec §4.2). An empty list cannot fail and is rejected by the check.

patterns_source.description: where the convention was read from

connection_env.description: Environment variable names holding the connection string, tried in order. There is deliberately no fallback literal (phase 2 spec §4.1): a connection string baked into a check is a credential in a repo. Nothing set, or nothing reachable, is exit 2 — could not run, never a pass.

schemas.description: The application schema(s). Declared, not inferred: a database also holds job-queue, warehouse and per-team sandbox schemas that are not the application's and are not this check's business.

schemas_reason.description: why this schema set is the application schema, and what was deliberately left out

tenant_columns.description: The repo's canonical tenant/context column names. Clause (b) of R-V8-07 — 'must contain no tenant-private facts' — is asserted at column level against this list. An empty list cannot fail and is refused.

tenant_columns_reason.description: where this list was read from

context_function_pattern.description: POSIX ERE matching this repo's RLS context functions. A policy counts as 'authenticated' only when its USING expression names one of them, so USING (true) and USING (is_active = true) do not qualify. Without this, 'authenticated' has no definition and clause (a) would pass on any policy at all.

global_vocabulary_tables.description: table name -> the recorded reason it is global vocabulary. Same shape as allow_fields_reasons, and required for the same reason: an entry with no reason is exit 2. Which tables count is a judgment R-V8-07 assumes and does not define, and §4.1 forbids inferring it from naming conventions.

global_vocabulary_source.description: How the set was determined, so the judgment is auditable rather than asserted. Refused if empty.

exempt_tables.description: table name -> the recorded reason it carries no RLS policy deliberately. Suppresses A1 (the 'has any policy at all' clause) for that table and nothing else: it cannot exempt a table from the global-vocabulary clauses, and a table listed here AND in global_vocabulary_tables is refused rather than resolved in some unpredictable order. Same shape and same rule as allow_fields_reasons — an entry with no reason is exit 2, and an entry naming a table that is not among those scanned is exit 2, because a config that no longer describes its schema has stopped describing anything. Exemptions are reported on PASS and FAIL alike; an exemption whose table has since acquired a policy is reported as stale.

zero_is_suspect_reason.description: Printed on a zero-violation result. A zero against a rule with recorded failures is suspect, not a pass (§9.5).
